prompt:
Use case: style-transfer. Make ONE finished transparent-background StarNet game prop from image 1, which is the binding ORIGINAL GEOMETRY GUIDE. Image 2 is the approved crate: use its restrained dark cool steel, broad readable plates, crisp worn bevels, very sparse warm brass catches, and subtle aged metal surface. Image 3 is station context only. Keep the guide’s precise overall silhouette/aspect, camera elevation, straight-on orthographic alignment, top-face depth, feet, open gaps, and every component/screen location. Reconstruct the coarse guide into refined painted game sprite detail; do not preserve giant pixel blocks. No new appendages, no taller/wider body, no perspective yaw or isometric diamond. Match the crate material density: broad clear forms, not ornate busy machinery. Functional glass MUST be smoked-black/OFF with no bright graphics; existing game code provides the exact animated pixels there. Keep dark glass rectangles in precisely their guide positions and sizes. Finish for tiny in-game legibility, not product photography. Entire single prop visible with tight balanced transparent margin; true transparent alpha, NO floor, ground/shadow scene, labels, text, humans, border, checkerboard illustration or second object.
Subject details: A narrow routing filter machine. Keep the single upright rectangular smoked-black inset centered over a shallow routing tray, its right projecting port and side bracket, and short base with two small muted brass catches. The central native purple/cyan pixels are a dynamic display REGION: preserve its geometry but render it as dark inactive glass. Do not replace it with a larger screen.
Geometry calibration: the complete opaque prop occupies 14 units wide by 19 units high. Keep its isolated SUBJECT width:height ratio exactly 0.7368, within 5%, before any margin; never make its body taller or wider. Preserve every original internal component position ratio. IMPORTANT: leave generous 10% fully transparent margin around ALL FOUR SIDES so no object edge is cut off. The guide is cropped tightly for measurement, but your output must not crop the object.

review.geometry: Within 8 percent native crop ratio; no edge clipping
